name: knee overview
title: A knee problem splits first on trauma: after an injury the mechanism and the swelling point to the structure, anterior cruciate ligament and meniscal tears from a pivot or twist on a planted foot, posterior cruciate, medial collateral and lateral collateral injuries from a blow; without trauma the site of the pain separates patellofemoral pain syndrome and knee bursitis in front, iliotibial band friction syndrome laterally and a popliteal cyst behind; each column gives presentation, the exam and workup, and treatment; the unhappy triad and knee injections are in panels

root.title: Knee problem: was there TRAUMA? If so, what was the MECHANISM and how fast did it SWELL? If not, WHERE does it hurt?
lines: every injury: history and exam first · X-ray to rule out a fracture (usually normal) · MRI only when the exam cannot decide
TRAUMA, swelling within 6 h: anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tear, fracture, patellar dislocation, large chondral injury
TRAUMA, swelling after 6 h: meniscal injury, posterior cruciate (PCL) injury, high-grade medial collateral (MCL) sprain, arthritis flare

groups.title: TRAUMA: PIVOT or TWIST on a planted foot
TRAUMA: A BLOW to the knee
lines: the direction of the force names the ligament

groups.title: NO trauma: FRONT of the knee
NO trauma: OUTSIDE of the knee

head: h
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tear
non-contact in 60–80%
female 4.5 : 1 · pivoting sports
inv: 2 · MRI if the exam is unsure
tx: back to sport 9–12 months after surgery

head: h
Meniscal tear
twisting with the foot planted
or degenerative with age
pres: Joint-line pain · DELAYED or on-and-off swelling
inv: 2 · MRI if conservative care fails or the tear is large
tx: 1 · Physiotherapy: range of motion, strengthen quadriceps + hamstrings
• bucket handle, root or large tear
White zone or chronic degenerative → RESECT

head: h
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) tear
blow to the front of the tibia, knee FLEXED (dashboard)
• or hyperextension
inv: 1 · Posterior drawer · sag sign · reverse Lachman
MRI if posterolateral corner injury suspected
tx: Rotatory instability or posterolateral corner → reconstruction

head: h
Medial collateral ligament (MCL) injury
VALGUS force, a collision
very common
pres: Medial pain · minimal to no swelling
• complete tear → look for an ACL tear
inv: Valgus stress on the flexed knee

head: h
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) injury
high-energy VARUS force
uncommon on its own
inv: Varus stress on the flexed knee
tx: Other injuries or instability → surgical repair

head: h
Patellofemoral pain syndrome
females, adolescents
↑ tibiofemoral angle and Q-angle
pres: • worse after activity and with prolonged sitting, stairs
inv: ~X-ray or MRI only if not responding to treatment

head: h
Knee bursitis
prepatellar · infrapatellar · suprapatellar
chronic friction
pres: Mild swelling + tenderness over the bursa
inv: Do not miss SEPTIC bursitis or trauma

head: h
Iliotibial band friction syndrome
band rubs the lateral femoral epicondyle below 30° of flexion
inv: • Ober's test POSITIVE: the leg stays up, with a gap between the knee and the table (tight IT band)

head: h
Popliteal (Baker's) cyst
synovial fluid through a defect in the back of the capsule
tx: Not settling, or vessel or nerve compromised
MRI + surgical referral, not just cyst removal

panels.title: Unhappy triad: VALGUS force on a flexed, externally rotated knee
items: the medial meniscus, attached to the MCL, tears next (bucket-handle tear)
abduction + external rotation + slight flexion then tears the ACL

panels.title: Knee injections
items: CORTICOSTEROID: rapid · < $20 · lasts < 4–12 weeks · may harm cartilage (weak evidence)
HYALURONIC ACID: > 26 weeks of relief · $300–500 · good safety
PLATELET-RICH PLASMA: $500–1,500 · no clinically significant benefit in trials
STEM CELLS: not shown better than other injections · Health Canada: a drug, needs formal approval
